title: Improve One Cause
outcome: By the end, I can repair one identified cause and rerun cases that previously passed.
scenario: A fictional quiet-activity chooser has a boundary bug and a proposed repair.
given: A: quiet Yes, 8 minutes; B: quiet No, 5 minutes. Request quiet required Yes.
U0 accepts only duration<available time. U1 fixes ≤ but accidentally removes the quiet requirement.

steps.label: Boundary failure
steps.detail: At 8 minutes, U0 rejects A and rejects noisy B: none.

steps.label: Expected repair
steps.detail: Correct logic must allow A when time equals 8.

steps.label: Regression case
steps.detail: At 6 quiet-required minutes, correct output is none.

steps.label: Bad revision
steps.detail: U1 selects noisy B at 6; fixing equality introduced a new failure.

explanation: A repair must preserve the full contract, not just make one failing example pass. The quiet condition and duration comparison are separate requirements. Changing only the inequality targets the recorded cause; removing the quiet check changes another behavior. Save previously passing cases to reveal such regressions.

counterfactual.change: Use U2, which changes < to ≤ and keeps the quiet check.
counterfactual.prediction: At 8 return A; at 6 return none.
counterfactual.reason: Equality is repaired while B remains ineligible because it is noisy.

student_task: Explain why “our repaired version now picks something” is not enough to show success at 6.
teacher_answer: Any chosen activity must be quiet and fit the time. B is noisy, so picking it violates the contract; none is the correct output.
project_evidence: Maintain sorter regression tests and compare complete version traces, retaining new failures rather than hiding them.
limits: Two examples establish only these outcomes; further cases are needed before generalising the repair.
review_note: Individually reviewed fictional topic example; arithmetic and declared policies checked. This is supported practice, not the reserved independent assessment.
